rationale: Fresh 3-lens review (blind/edge-case/acceptance, all 3 ran) of the uncommitted diff fixing the 3 regressions confirmed in a reviewer's follow-up comment on top of commit dd337fe0 (vendor/split-host providers permanently losing identity, repo-local workspace retargeting a global profile's pre-migration-008 fallback, and `codemie profile list` showing one shared URL for every global profile). The edge-case lens surfaced a real critical bug introduced by this same diff: resolveProfileWorkspace()'s new per-profile fallback only trusted the caller-supplied `profileIdentity` param, but the new `codemie profile list` call site passes an empty one, so a profile that already owns its own identity could have it silently overwritten by a stale/leftover shared workspace value whenever canUseSharedIdentity() found no positive conflict evidence — reintroducing a narrower form of the exact bug this whole ticket exists to fix. The acceptance lens separately found that canUseSharedIdentity()'s new doc comment falsely claimed statusline.ts mirrors the same guard, when statusline.ts still ran the old blanket origin-only check. Both were fixed inline during this review round (not deferred): resolveProfileWorkspace() now also checks the looked-up ownProfile's own identity independently of what the caller passed, the `profile list` call site now also passes each profile's own identity explicitly (defense in depth), and statusline.ts's inline fallback was rewritten to mirror canUseSharedIdentity()'s provider-gate + sibling-evidence logic exactly, making the doc comment's claim true. 2 new regression tests were added for the critical fix and 2 more for the statusline alignment, all written test-first (confirmed RED before the fix, GREEN after). 8 other blind-lens concerns were investigated and dismissed as either false positives (profile-list name collision — listProfiles() already dedupes local/global by name before this code runs, confirmed by direct read) or accepted, documented design trade-offs/pre-existing characteristics with no new behavioral impact (the lone-mismatched-profile permissive default; the per-call config re-read's minor performance cost; leftover workspace data when no profile claims it). After the fixes: full unit suite 5905 passed/2 skipped, typecheck clean, lint clean (--max-warnings=0), build clean including the statusline esbuild bundle. No `defer` or `dismiss` findings are emitted per the blocker-only findings contract; 8 lower-severity observations were filtered as noted above.

business_review.item: AC1: each global profile stores/resolves its own identity independently
business_review.notes: Unaffected by this diff's parameter plumbing; own-identity precedence in load() unchanged.

business_review.item: AC2: switching profiles applies the selected profile's own identity
business_review.notes: selectedProfileName threaded through load()/loadWithSources() into resolveProfileWorkspace(); own identity still wins via removeUndefined merge.

business_review.item: AC3: identity fields not overwritten across unrelated global profiles
business_review.notes: canUseSharedIdentity() only allows cross-profile fallback absent positive conflict evidence; resolveProfileWorkspace() now also independently trusts the looked-up profile's own identity regardless of caller input (fixed this round).

business_review.item: AC4: resolveProfileWorkspace() resolves identity from profile-specific data, not shared mutable workspace state
business_review.notes: Fallback sourced explicitly from loadMultiProviderConfig().workspace (global), gated by canUseSharedIdentity() and now also by the profile's own already-known identity.

business_review.item: AC5: isLocalProfile branch of resolveProfileWorkspace() must not change
AC6: non-identity WORKSPACE_KEYS remain scope-level shared
business_review.notes: result seeded with `{...workspace}`; only IDENTITY_KEYS are touched per key.

business_review.item: AC7: two global profiles targeting different CodeMie environments resolve independently
business_review.notes: Covered by canUseSharedIdentity()'s sibling-claim logic; new migration tests (medecision/env-b) exercise this.

business_review.item: AC8: switching back to the first profile restores its own identity
business_review.notes: Not touched beyond parameter plumbing; own-identity precedence mechanism unchanged.

business_review.item: Migration 008 remains idempotent and never destroys data nobody claimed
business_review.notes: `if (!anyChanged) return config;` guard added; new test 'keeps workspace when every profile already has its own identity or every candidate was refused' confirms.

business_review.item: CLAIM 1: vendor-subscription / split-host ai-run-sso profiles must not permanently lose pre-008 shared identity fallback
business_review.notes: canUseSharedIdentity() gates on isCodeMiePlatformProvider() first; vendor providers and lone split-host profiles are always allowed. New tests cover config.ts, migration 008, and statusline.ts.

business_review.item: CLAIM 1 corollary: the same guard must be consistent everywhere it is duplicated (statusline.ts)
business_review.notes: Initially FAIL in the first review pass — statusline.ts still ran the old blanket origin-match with no provider/sibling gating, contradicting canUseSharedIdentity()'s own doc comment. Fixed this round: statusline.ts now has its own inline canUseSharedIdentity() mirroring config.ts's exactly, used in resolveBudget()'s fallback. 2 new tests added; all 107 statusline tests pass.

business_review.item: CLAIM 2: pre-008 read-time fallback must source identity only from the global shared workspace, never a repo-local workspace
business_review.notes: resolveProfileWorkspace() re-fetches `workspace` from loadMultiProviderConfig() (global) for the identity fallback, separately from resolveWorkspace(workingDir) used for non-identity keys. New test with a conflicting repo-local workspace confirms the global value wins.

business_review.item: CLAIM 3: `codemie profile list` must show each global profile's own resolved codeMieUrl, not one shared value for the whole list
business_review.notes: listProfiles() now loops per profile, passing both profileName and the profile's own known identity into resolveProfileWorkspace(); display.ts keys the fallback map by profile name. New test asserts two global profiles format with distinct URLs.

business_review.item: canUseSharedIdentity(profile, siblingProfiles, ownName, sharedCodeMieUrl) refuses only when all 3 stated conditions hold
business_review.notes: Implementation matches its doc comment 1:1, confirmed by direct read and by the migration/config/statusline test suites.
